necessary_context.content: Definition 1: F_p(Delta,L_p) is the union over finite d in N of C-infinity functions on R^d with f(0)-inf f<=Delta and L_p-Lipschitz pth derivatives. The source defines smoothness using every unit direction v and line restriction f_{x,v}(t)=f(x+tv): |f_{x,v}^{(p)}(t)-f_{x,v}^{(p)}(t')|<=L_p|t-t'| for all x,t,t'. F_{1:p} is the intersection over q<=p. Vector norm is Euclidean.
necessary_context.locator: Section 2.1, Definition 1, PDF p.4; notation p.3
necessary_context.name: Function class and smoothness convention

necessary_context.applies_to: Theorem 2 and its Oracle Complexity interpretation
necessary_context.content: A_det^(1) permits arbitrary measurable deterministic updates from previous function-value and gradient responses, separately for each finite dimension. A_zr^(1) requires supp(x^(t)) subset of the union of supp(grad f(x^(s))) for s<t, hence x^(1)=0. T_epsilon(A,f) is the first iterate index t with ||grad f(x^(t))||<=epsilon, and T_epsilon(A,F)=inf_{A in A} sup_{f in F} T_epsilon(A,f).
necessary_context.locator: Sections 2.2–2.3, equation (3) and equation (4), PDF pp.4–5
necessary_context.name: Algorithm classes and hitting complexity

necessary_context.content: For an orthogonally invariant function class, Proposition 1 transfers the zero-respecting lower bound to all deterministic first-order algorithms. This uses dimension freedom and a resisting rotation; the explicit unrotated chain alone imposes support restrictions only on zero-respecting iterates.
necessary_context.locator: Section 2.4, Observation 1 and Proposition 1, PDF pp.5–6
necessary_context.name: Deterministic lifting
